::: {.laser-introduction}
## Introduction

Quality assurance of co-registration in XY and Z verifies whether multiple fluorescence channels are spatially aligned as expected. Even small chromatic shifts can distort overlay images, misrepresent co-localization, and compromise quantitative distance measurements.

Routine monitoring with multicolor reference samples helps detect alignment drift and supports spatially accurate, reproducible imaging.
:::

## What is assessed

### Lateral registration

The XY positions of the same reference objects are compared across fluorescence channels. The lateral magnitude shows how closely channels remain registered within the image plane.

### Axial registration

The focal position of each channel is compared along Z. The signed axial offset preserves the direction of displacement relative to the designated reference channel.

::: {.qa-method-note}
#### Reading the chromatic-aberration dashboards

Shift vectors are displayed in nanometers relative to the 488 nm reference channel. The lateral plot shows the XY vector magnitude; hover details preserve the signed X and Y components. The axial plot shows the signed Z component. Use each objective dashboard to compare channels and follow registration over time.
:::
